I finally figured out what I did wrong in Step 7 --- a simple typo -- I can't believe it !

> upper case on the 2nd "M"  -- wrong:
> > LoadModule R_Module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
> should be:
> > LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
>
Also I re-did the configure in Step 5 using this (from http://rapache.net/manual.html) and it helped:

./configure \
    --with-R=/usr/bin/R \
    --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/bin/apxs2 \
Also here are some more typos in the steps that I fixed:

>
> STEP #8:
> Install the brew package
> sudo R

> install.packages( "brew", lib = "usr/lib/R/lib" )
>
> STEP #9:
> Restart Apache2

> here has mentioned that running the same process via CLI (in absence of

messages.body_plain:
Its probably related to your old version of glibc or so. We have seen similar problems (search the mailing list) before with old versions of centos and debian. They disappear when upgraded to a newer distribution.

I highly recommend Ubuntu 12.04 for R and rApache. RHEL has no native support for R, so I suppose you pulled R from EPEL or so, but R and many of its packages assume relatively relatively recent versions of libraries. I have had many problems before with R on CentOS and recommend to avoid it when possible. If you want to stick with the Redhat family, use Fedora.

On Wed, Aug 8, 2012 at 2:05 PM, Ken Williams <ken.wi...@clearcapital.com> wrote:

> We have some job submissions to an rApache program and about 20% of the time these fail.
> I've been troubleshooting this issue for a few days now and traced the failures to segmentation faults in the httpd error_log.
>
> We're have the same issues on 5 nodes with identical configurations.
>
> I've been testing against a single node, and since I have updated to the latest patch sets from CentOS5. I also updated R to 2.15.1 and compiled the latest rapache as of 8/7/2012 via git.
>
> I've also gone as far as to install apache 2.2.22 from source tarball and again, recompile rapache from source.
>
> I'm not sure if this is a code issue, and honestly I'm not an R developer so I'm not sure how to make that determination. The R developer on staff here has mentioned that running the same process via CLI (in absence of rapache) the code executes fine and doesn't segfault. This leads me to believe the issue is somewhere in rapache land...
>
> Any advice/assistance would be welcomed!
>
> Thanks,
> -Ken Williams

> Its probably related to your old version of glibc or so. We have seen similar problems (search the mailing list) before with old versions of centos and debian. They disappear when upgraded to a newer distribution.
>
> I highly recommend Ubuntu 12.04 for R and rApache. RHEL has no native support for R, so I suppose you pulled R from EPEL or so, but R and many of its packages assume relatively relatively recent versions of libraries. I have had many problems before with R on CentOS and recommend to avoid it when possible. If you want to stick with the Redhat family, use Fedora.

messages.subject: Re: looking to contract somebody to help stand up a R web app
messages.subject_clean: looking to contract somebody to help stand up a R web app
messages.body_plain:
Dear Markus,

we are currently working on a web application (building on RApache) which is likely to be useful in your case.

The webapp would deal with the back-end (storing data in DB, handling users and permissions, loading required packages, an editor to create statistical templates, rendering R output in HTML/pdf/docx format etc.), so users can concentrate solely on R and the output is automatically rendered in an IMHO pretty way.

We are using some of our quite new packages building on Pandoc's markdown, so by visiting our project pages, you might get an insight how you can run R code in our forthcoming application and also how the R output would be rendered:
pander <http://rapporter.github.com/pander/> is a wrapper around Pandoc <http://johnmacfarlane.net/pandoc/> and also provides a modified version of `brew` (I am pretty sure all list member know about this latter) which renders R objects in markdown with the option to export all those to HTML/docx/odt/pdf etc. including all the generated plots
and rapport <http://rapport-package.info/> building on `pander` provides a way to create statistical templates to be run against any user specified data with optional parameters
If you are interested in this project (estimated start: in the middle of September), please visit our signup page at rapporter.net <http://rapporter.net>.
Do not be deterred by the minimal description crowded with some marketing slogans, users will definitely have the option to create custom templates (running any R code) with a fool-proof GUI to let even non useRs also enjoy your algorithms and the results :)

I hope you would find that service (and my current message) useful, I could provide some public demos of the application on demand.

Best,
Gergely

I am good with R and can usually hack through building a web page, but putting together a working R web app felt like it was over my head.  I got a version of rapache to work on a linux machine and feed it simple server requests, but was completely lost when it came connecting a proper front end.

I think once the app is setup and working at a simple level, I will be able to work on updating and improving the front end and R code as necessary.

> Looking for any suggestions on who to talk to and how much something like this might cost.  Also, should I be looking at the Revolution Analytics Web Services API?  Is that possibly a simpler solution for me?

> Markus
